Fact:
2024 Medicaid Improper Payment Rate: The estimated rate was 5.09%, according to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities.

The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities highlights that the legislation is estimated to cut Medicaid by over $900 billion, potentially putting 9.9 million to 14.9 million people at risk of losing Medicaid coverage. They also point out that an earlier version of the bill had a provision for work requirements that could have caused 5.2 million adults to lose Medicaid, and many analysts believe this number could be higher in the final legislation, as the work requirement was expanded to include parents with children over 13.

The Association of State and Territorial Health Officials similarly reports the CBO estimate of 11.8 million people losing health coverage by 2034 due to the health provisions of the bill, with an additional 5.1 million potentially losing coverage due to other policy changes outside the bill itself.

The Center for American Progress states the CBO estimated the bill would cut federal spending on Medicaid and CHIP by $1.02 trillion, leading to at least 10.5 million people being eliminated from the programs by 2034. They also project that approximately 16 million people could end up uninsured due to the bill, encompassing losses from both Medicaid and other health programs
